newsitem.title: USA: EIA sees record 8.1 mln bpd US summer gasoline use.
newsitem.headline: EIA sees record 8.1 mln bpd US summer gasoline use.

text.p: U.S. gasoline demand this summer is expected to rise to a record 8.14 million barrels per day, up 1.8 percent from last summer, the Energy Information Administration said Thursday.
But with lower crude prices, gasoline pump prices should hold at one to two cents below last summer's levels at an average of $1.31 per gallon through the summer.

To meet the demand growth, "much hinges on the ability of U.S. refiners to step up gasoline production levels to new highs, and on the continued availability of foreign supplies suitable for the U.S. market," EIA said.
EIA forecast that gasoline production during the summer driving season -- the second and third quarters -- would average 7.83 million bpd, up 2.2 percent from last summer.
Net gasoline imports were projected to average 318,000 bpd through this summer, the same as a year ago.

Gasoline stocks at the end of the third quarter were expected to fall to 196.5 million barrels, about four million barrels lower than last year's level, which EIA said reflected refiners' reluctance to hold inventory when prices could fall.
"The U.S. summer gasoline market is therefore expected to be balanced but fairly tight," the agency said in its summer gasoline outlook.
Gasoline prices could top last summer's high levels "if refiners run into production problems or imports turn out to be less available than projected," it said.
U.S. national prices last summer peaked in May at $1.38 per gallon on the back of surging crude oil markets.
EIA attributed the growth in demand this year, more than double last year's pace, to greater highway travel spurred by fattened incomes and lower gasoline prices.
The forecast assumed that U.S. Gross Domestic Product would grow 2.8 percent this year and imported oil prices would average $19.66 per barrel this summer, down from $20.41 last summer.
